Compare Analytical Results Among Groups

Source: R/stats.R
compare_groups.Rd

Performs multiple-group statistical comparisons on environmental analytical results.

Usage

compare_groups(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
compare_groups(
  df,
  location_id = "location_id",
  param_name = "param_name",
  sample_date = "sample_date",
  analysis_result = "analysis_result",
  default_unit = "default_unit",
  compare = location_id,
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'grouped_df'
compare_groups(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
compare_groups(
  df,
  compare = NULL,
  result_col = NULL,
  censored_col = NULL,
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

anova_test(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
anova_test(
  df,
  location = "location_id",
  analyte = "param_name",
  sample_date = "sample_date",
  result = "analysis_result",
  unit = "default_unit",
  compare = location,
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
anova_test(
  df,
  compare = location_var(df),
  result_col = analysis_result_var(df),
  censored_col = censored_var(df),
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

welch_test(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
welch_test(
  df,
  location = "location_id",
  analyte = "param_name",
  sample_date = "sample_date",
  result = "analysis_result",
  unit = "default_unit",
  compare = location,
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
welch_test(
  df,
  compare = location_var(df),
  result_col = analysis_result_var(df),
  censored_col = censored_var(df),
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

kruskal_test(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
kruskal_test(
  df,
  location = "location_id",
  analyte = "param_name",
  sample_date = "sample_date",
  result = "analysis_result",
  unit = "default_unit",
  compare = location,
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
kruskal_test(
  df,
  compare = location_var(df),
  result_col = analysis_result_var(df),
  censored_col = censored_var(df),
  keep_data_object = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

compare

Character column name identifying the grouping factor to compare.

keep_data_object

Logical indicating whether the complete statistical test object should be retained in the returned output.

result_col

Analytical result column.

variance_alpha

Significance level used by Levene's test to determine whether group variances are considered unequal. Defaults to `0.05`.

levene_center

Centering method for Levene's test. `"median"` performs the Brown-Forsythe version and is the default. `"mean"` performs the classical mean-centered version.

Value

A tibble containing one row per comparison group.

The returned table includes:

comparison_method

Statistical procedure used.

statistic

Test statistic returned by the selected procedure.

p_value

P-value associated with the test statistic.

test

Full statistical test object when `keep_data_object = TRUE`.

Details

`compare_groups()` automatically selects a recommended comparison procedure using [derive_decision()] and [statistical_decision()].

Recommended methods are based primarily on the degree of censoring:

  • `anova` for low-censoring datasets

  • `kruskal` for moderate or high censoring

  • `insufficient_data` when too few observations are available

Explicit alternatives are available through:

  • [anova_test()]

  • [welch_test()]

  • [kruskal_test()]

Existing grouping created with [dplyr::group_by()] is respected. Comparisons are performed independently within each grouping level.

For ungrouped `env_schema` objects, comparisons are performed separately for each analyte and analysis unit.

Automatic method selection follows the active [statistical_decision()] framework.

Under the default EPA-style profile:

ConditionVariance testRecommendationMethod
<15% censoredp >= alphaEqual varianceANOVA
<15% censoredp < alphaUnequal varianceWelch
15-90%Not usedNonparametric comparisonKruskal-Wallis
>=90%Not usedInsufficient informationNo comparison

Comparisons require at least two distinct comparison groups.

If the comparison variable contains only one level, test statistics and p-values are returned as `NA`.

The comparison variable cannot also be an active grouping variable.

Existing grouping controls the strata within which comparisons are performed.

For example:


gw |>
  dplyr::group_by(param_name) |>
  compare_groups(compare = "location_id")

compares locations separately within each analyte.


gw |>
  dplyr::group_by(well_class) |>
  compare_groups(compare = "location_id")

compares locations separately within each well classification.

Under the default EPA-style guidance profile, `compare_groups()` recommends classical ANOVA for low-censored datasets and Kruskal-Wallis tests for datasets with moderate or high censoring.

Explicit method-selection functions are available for users who wish to override the automatic recommendation framework:

  • [anova_test()]

  • [welch_test()]

  • [kruskal_test()]

ANOVA Method

`anova_test()` performs a classical one-way analysis of variance using [stats::aov()].

This method assumes:

  • approximately normal residuals

  • homogeneous variances among groups

  • independent observations

This function bypasses automatic method selection and always performs ANOVA.

Welch Method

`welch_test()` performs Welch's unequal-variance analysis of variance using [stats::oneway.test()].

Welch's ANOVA relaxes the equal-variance assumption required by classical ANOVA and is provided as an explicit analyst override.

This method is not selected automatically by [compare_groups()].

Kruskal-Wallis Method

`kruskal_test()` performs a Kruskal-Wallis rank-sum test using [stats::kruskal.test()].

This nonparametric method is appropriate when normality or variance assumptions are not satisfied and is commonly recommended for datasets with moderate or extensive censoring.

This function bypasses automatic method selection and always performs a Kruskal-Wallis comparison.

See also

[statistical_decision()], [derive_decision()], [anova_test()], [welch_test()], [kruskal_test()]
